title: Sticky shift notes — Sofia (coffee shift)
content:
Sticky shift notes (6:45–14:45) — quick brain-dump for handoff

Quick summary:
- Pages: 3 total (2 P1/P2s).
- Resolved: Latency surge in hosted-api-us-east-1 (partial mitigation).
- In progress: KV-cache evictions causing incoherent chat sessions (need deeper trace).
- Runbook gaps discovered: cache invalidation steps unclear for autoscale path.

Incident: hosted-api-us-east-1 token latency spike (P2 -> P1-ish when load spiked)
- Timeline:
  - 07:10: first pager: 99th pct latency jumped from ~120ms to 800ms.
  - 07:12: rolled routing to fallback region (us-west-2) for affected customers via routing policy.
  - 07:17: discovered a backlog on the gpu pool (dedicated nodes hitting high kernel queuing).
  - 07:30: scaled up dedicated pool + increased batching-window temporarily; latency improved to ~180ms.
- Actions I took:
  - toggled autoscale policy for dedicated pool (note: console UI path slow)
  - added temporary override to routing policy: prefer us-west-2 for model-x until next deploy.
  - left annotation on incident ticket INFRA-513 with commands and logs.
- Short term mitigations to keep: keep routing override for 1h, monitor queue length metric (routing.queue_depth).
- Next steps / followups:
  - [ ] Add a preflight check in the autoscaler to avoid simultaneous draining + scaling (ticket: INFRA-613).
  - [ ] Confirm with infra team whether kernel preemption patch in kernel-ops had side effects (ping @Arjun).

Incident: KV cache evictions -> chat context mismatch (ongoing)
- Observed behavior: several customer sessions lost earlier conversation turns, model responded with unrelated context. Correlated with eviction spikes and autoscaler events.
- Hypothesis: autoscaling teardown triggers KV cache flushes without graceful handoff; some request routing uses stale cache-key mappings leading to repeated full attention hits.
- Evidence:
  - timeline aligns with autoscaler cycle at 09:02, 09:32, 09:58.
  - logs: runtime:cache:evict entries with reason=OOM and source=scale_down.
  - sample request traces: trace IDs in slack thread #sre-kv-trace (see linked artifacts).
- Immediate actions:
  - reduced aggressive scale-down threshold to 20% for the affected pool (temporary).
  - added extra logging for cache handoff: env DEBUG_CACHE_HANDOFF=1 on canary.
- Runbook gap: no clear steps to coordinate KV cache handoff across instances during scaling. Needs a documented handoff protocol (see Runbook TODOs).

Runbook TODOs (high priority)
- [ ] Add explicit step for cache handoff in "Autoscaler and Node Lifecycle" runbook: including signal to draining nodes to persist KV to shared cache or transfer ownership. (owner: Sofia)
- [ ] Add a metric and alert for cache_eviction_rate with per-pool granularity. (owner: Lena)
- [ ] Update playbook commands for manual routing override with exact CLI flags (so next oncall doesn't rely on console). Example CLI snippet to document:
    rwdctl routing set-priority --model model-x --region us-west-2 --duration 60m --reason "latency mitigation"
- [ ] Postmortem template: capture whether batching-window changes contributed to kernel queueing. (owner: Arjun)

Commands I ran (notes for followup / reproducibility)
- Applied temporary routing override:
  - rwdctl routing set-priority --model model-x --region us-west-2 --duration 60m --reason "latency mitigation"
- Scale policy tweak:
  - rwdctl autoscale update --pool gpu-dedicated-01 --min-instances 4 --scale-down-threshold 20
- Cache debug toggles (canary):
  - kubectl -n runtime exec -it pod/runtime-canary -- bash -c 'export DEBUG_CACHE_HANDOFF=1 && supervisorctl restart runtime'
- Pulled traces:
  - curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TRACE_TOKEN" "https://traces.internal.redwood/api/v1/trace?trace_id=abc123" | jq '.segments[] | {span,latency}'

Handoff notes for next shift
- Keep routing override until autoscaler behavior verified (check routing.queue_depth every 5m).
- Follow up with infra on kernel queuing change (Arjun to sync).
- Push cache handoff logging to staging and run k-sim scale tests (scale to 2 -> 30 nodes) and capture eviction rates.
- Followup ticket: LIN-742 for adding per-pool eviction metric + alert.

Things I scribbled / quick ideas
- Could we add a "graceful-kv-handoff" annotation to K8s pods so termination flow triggers a KV snapshot to shared redis? Tradeoff: snapshot latency vs safety.
- Consider soft-eviction: mark entries stale and let new instance rebuild gradually instead of hard delete.

Quick checklist to close before leaving
- [ ] Push cache-handoff debug to staging (PR exists: runtime PR #1248 but needs small env change).
- [ ] Confirm monitoring dashboard shows per-pool eviction rate (dashboard: "Cache Health - per pool")
- [ ] Leave clear handoff note in the incident ticket and Slack (#inc-513-thread)

Notes to self / reminders
- Email infra lead for kernel change impact (subject: "kernel preemption patch — observed queue stalls 2026-10-09")
- Block time tomorrow 08:00–09:30 to run scale tests with Arjun.
- Draft small tech note for product about routing fallback behavior for Dedicated vs Hosted (short, 2 bullets).

Open questions
- Does the autoscaler ever call drain hooks that our runtime ignores? (I think yes, but need to prove)
- If we snapshot KV to redis on termination, what's the cost curve for big models with 20k keys? Need back-of-envelope.

Slack / threads / references
- #sre-incidents — thread started 07:12 "us-east-1 latency" (search term: "latency surge model-x 2026-10-09")
- Incident ticket: INFRA-513 (linked above)
- Runtime PR to watch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1248 (cache handoff logging)

Handoff blurb to paste into Slack for next oncall:
- "Heads up — kept routing override to us-west-2 for model-x after latency surge this morning. KV-cache evictions observed during autoscale; I reduced scale-down aggressiveness and enabled canary logging. Please monitor routing.queue_depth and cache_eviction_rate (LIN-742). Full notes in INFRA-513. — Sofia"

End of notes.
